properties.subtype: farm or neighbourhood lane (traced from the period map)
properties.name: Trostle-Weikert-Swisher Lane, Emmitsburg Road to the Codori-Trostle woodlot (drawn as a double dashed lane)
properties.period_note: From Emmitsburg Road past the Abraham Trostle farmstead into the Codori-Trostle woodlot (where it met a woodlot lane); north through the woodlot, then east through the George Weikert farmstead, north-east through the north end of the Swisher-Patterson woodlot to the Taneytown Road nearly opposite the M. Fry house. Western and eastern sections improved, the woodlot section a cart path. Status today: western half is United States Avenue (realigned 1935-43 in front of the Trostle barn); eastern half disused and mostly gone (an NPS horse trail follows its corridor)

sources.cite: Treatment Philosophy: The 1863 Landscape, Gettysburg NMP (NPS, 2004), ch. 2-3 (circulation, fencing, water features)
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Route of the Trostle-Weikert-Swisher Lane as above (1872 Warren Survey Map sections 03 and 04); an important avenue of approach for Union units on 1 and 2 July; the western half has become United States Avenue.

sources.cite: Cultural Landscapes Inventory: Emmitsburg Road Ridge Battlefield, Gettysburg NMP (2024), citing CLR draft 2000 and CLR 2002
sources.quote_or_paraphrase: Trostle Lane extended from Emmitsburg Road past Weikert's farm to the Taneytown Road following a circuitous route; the western half was incorporated into United States Avenue (completed 1895) and the eastern half fell into disuse, eventually disappearing.
